result.markdown: --- title: "Session 5 — Assumptions and Reporting" subtitle: "Proportional hazards · Schoenfeld residuals · strata and time-split fixes · censoring · reporting · Lab 5" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Session 4: the Cox model and hazard ratios - Today: **can we trust a single hazard ratio?** - By the end you can: - **test and plot** the proportional-hazards assumption - **fix** a violation by **stratifying** or **splitting time** - judge whether **censoring** is acceptable - **report** a survival analysis ::: # Topic 1 — Proportional hazards {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## The assumption ::: {.key} The Cox model assumes the **hazard ratio is constant over time**. If one group is worse **early** and the same **later**, a single HR averages two different stories. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fit <- coxph(Surv(time_months, status) ~ age + sex + hiv + diabetes + smoker + bmi + mdr_tb + smear + treatment, data = tb) zph <- cox.zph(fit) round(zph$table, 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` chisq df p age 5.785 1 0.016 sex 0.008 1 0.928 hiv 0.276 1 0.600 diabetes 1.293 1 0.256 smoker 1.677 1 0.195 bmi 3.970 1 0.046 mdr_tb 0.022 1 0.881 smear 15.317 1 0.000 treatment 2.734 1 0.098 GLOBAL 30.465 9 0.000 ``` ::: ::: ## Reading the test ::: {.incremental} - `cox.zph()` tests whether **Schoenfeld residuals** trend with time, **one p-value per term** plus a global one - **smear** has a very small p-value: its effect **changes over time** - With nine terms tested, **borderline** p-values (age, BMI) can be **chance**: **look at the plot** before acting ::: ## Look at it ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(zph[8]); abline(h = 0, col = "red") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s5_assumptions_reporting_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - A **flat line** means a constant log hazard ratio - Here the curve **slopes down**: strong effect early, little later - A second look: **log-log plot** of the curves; **parallel** lines support proportional hazards ::: # Topic 2 — Fixing a violation {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Fix 1: stratify ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} cox_strat <- coxph(Surv(time_months, status) ~ age + sex + hiv + diabetes + smoker + bmi + mdr_tb + treatment + strata(smear), data = tb) round(exp(coef(cox_strat)), 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` age sexMale hivPositive diabetesYes smokerYes bmi 1.02 1.07 2.01 1.33 1.10 0.91 mdr_tbYes treatmentDOT 2.36 0.57 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - `strata(smear)`: a **separate baseline hazard** for each group, so the other HRs are not distorted - **You lose** an HR for smear itself, which is a reasonable price if smear is only a **nuisance** variable - Use for a **categorical** variable ::: ## Fix 2: split time and estimate the effect in each period ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tb_split <- survSplit(Surv(time_months, status) ~ ., data = tb, cut = 6, episode = "period") tb_split$smear_pos <- as.numeric(tb_split$smear == "Positive") cox_split <- coxph(Surv(tstart, time_months, status) ~ age + sex + hiv + diabetes + smoker + bmi + mdr_tb + treatment + smear_pos:factor(period), data = tb_split) round(exp(coef(cox_split))[c("smear_pos:factor(period)1", "smear_pos:factor(period)2")], 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` smear_pos:factor(period)1 smear_pos:factor(period)2 3.28 0.58 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} "Smear-positive disease **tripled the hazard in the first 6 months** (HR about 3) and was **not harmful afterwards** (HR about 0.6)." The **effect of time** is itself a finding. Other options: **time-varying covariates**, **landmark analysis**, **parametric models**. ::: # Topic 3 — Censoring and reporting {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Is censoring "non-informative"? ::: {.incremental} - Kaplan-Meier and Cox assume patients **censored at time t** have the **same future risk** as those who remain - If the **sickest** are **lost to follow-up**, the curve is **too optimistic** - Check: **how many** were lost, **who** (compare groups), and **when** - **Sensitivity analysis:** treat everyone lost as dead (worst case) and as alive (best case) ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tb |> group_by(hiv) |> summarise(n = n(), pct_lost = round(100 * mean(censor_reason %in% "Lost to follow-up"), 1)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 2 × 3 hiv n pct_lost 1 Negative 537 17.3 2 Positive 63 15.9 ``` ::: ::: ## Other threats | Problem | What to do | |---|---| | **Competing risks** (death from another cause stops the event of interest) | cumulative incidence (`tidycmprsk`), Fine-Gray model; beyond this workshop | | **Immortal time bias** (time before exposure counted as exposed) | define **time zero** carefully; time-varying exposure | | **Different time zero** for groups | use the **same** starting point (e.g. start of treatment) | | **Too many covariates** for the events | fewer predictors; shrinkage | ## Reporting checklist ::: {.good} 1. **Population, time zero, event, end of follow-up**; number of patients, events, censored 2. **Median follow-up** (reverse KM) and **reasons for censoring** 3. **Kaplan-Meier** curves with number at risk; survival at fixed times with CI 4. **Cox model:** crude and adjusted HRs with CI, reference groups, units 5. **Proportional-hazards check** and what you did about violations 6. **Limitations:** informative censoring, competing risks, confounding, **association, not cause** ::: ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 5 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `survival-workshop/labs/lab5_assumptions.R` - `cox.zph()` · plot the Schoenfeld residuals · log-log plot - `strata()` and `survSplit()` fixes - lost to follow-up by group · final hazard-ratio table ::: **Time:** 40 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s5q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="tkkmp0.4t433a" data-show="VGhlIGhhemFyZCByYXRpbyBmb3Igc21lYXIgaXMgbm90IGNvbnN0YW50IG92ZXIgZm9sbG93 LXVwIHRpbWU=" data-explain="QSBzbWFsbCBwLXZhbHVlIG1lYW5zIFNjaG9lbmZlbGQgcmVzaWR1YWxzIHRyZW5kIHdpdGgg dGltZSwgc28gdGhlIEhSIGNoYW5nZXMgb3ZlciBmb2xsb3ctdXAuIEl0IHNheXMgdGhlIHBy b3BvcnRpb25hbC1oYXphcmRzIGFzc3VtcHRpb24gZmFpbHMgZm9yIHRoYXQgdGVybSwgbm90 IHRoYXQgdGhlIGVmZmVjdCBpcyBudWxsLg=="} cox.zph() gives p = 0.0001 for the smear-status term. What does this mean? - Smear status has no effect on survival at any time during follow-up - The Cox model cannot be fitted to these data until smear is removed - The hazard ratio for smear is not constant over follow-up time - Smear status should be removed from the data set before analysis ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s5q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="tkkzxo.4t4hkm" data-show="U3RyYXRpZnkgdGhlIG1vZGVsIGJ5IHRoYXQgdmFyaWFibGU=" data-explain="U3RyYXRpZnlpbmcgZ2l2ZXMgZWFjaCBsZXZlbCBpdHMgb3duIGJhc2VsaW5lIGhhemFyZCwg c28gdGhlIG90aGVyIGhhemFyZCByYXRpb3MgYXJlIG5vdCBkaXN0b3J0ZWQuIFRoZSBwcmlj ZSBpcyB0aGF0IG5vIEhSIGlzIGVzdGltYXRlZCBmb3IgdGhlIHN0cmF0aWZ5aW5nIHZhcmlh YmxlIGl0c2VsZi4="} Which is an appropriate response to a proportional-hazards violation for a nuisance categorical variable? - Delete the variable and report nothing about it - Stratify the model by that variable - Treat the variable as a continuous variable - Use a t-test for each time period ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s5q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="tkld6e.4t4w20" data-show="VGhlIHNtZWFyIGVmZmVjdCByZXZlcnNlcyBvdmVyIHRpbWUsIHNvIG9uZSBIUiB3b3VsZCBt aXNsZWFk" data-explain="U3BsaXR0aW5nIHRpbWUgc2hvd3MgdGhlIGhhemFyZCBkaWZmZXJzIGJ5IHBlcmlvZC4gQSBz aW5nbGUgYXZlcmFnZSBIUiBoaWRlcyB0aGF0IHRoZSBlYXJseSBleGNlc3MgcmlzayBkaXNh cHBlYXJzIGxhdGVyLg=="} In the time-split analysis the smear HR is about 3 for the first 6 months and about 0.6 afterwards. What is the best summary? - Smear status has an average hazard ratio of about 1.8 over follow-up - The result is a computing error, as hazard ratios cannot be below 1 - The smear effect reverses over time, so one HR would mislead - Smear status is unrelated to survival, as the two values cancel out ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s5q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="tklqf4.4t5aje" data-show="SWYgdGhvc2UgbG9zdCB3ZXJlIHNpY2tlciwgdGhlIGN1cnZlIGlzIHRvbyBvcHRpbWlzdGlj " data-explain="VGhlIG1ldGhvZCBhc3N1bWVzIGNlbnNvcmVkIHBhdGllbnRzIGhhdmUgdGhlIHNhbWUgZnV0 dXJlIHJpc2sgYXMgdGhvc2Ugd2hvIHJlbWFpbi4gSWYgdGhlIHBhdGllbnRzIGxvc3Qgd2Vy ZSBhdCBoaWdoZXIgcmlzaywgc3Vydml2YWwgaXMgb3ZlcmVzdGltYXRlZC4="} Why can a large number lost to follow-up threaten a Kaplan-Meier analysis? - Patients lost to follow-up are removed from the numerator and denominator - Kaplan-Meier cannot handle any censored patients - Loss to follow-up lowers the p-value of the log-rank test - If those lost were sicker, the curve is too optimistic ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s5q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="tkm3nq.4t5p0o" data-show="TWVkaWFuIGZvbGxvdy11cCwgZXZlbnRzIGFuZCB0aGUgcHJvcG9ydGlvbmFsLWhhemFyZHMg Y2hlY2s=" data-explain="QSByZWFkZXIgbmVlZHMgcGF0aWVudHMsIGV2ZW50cywgY2Vuc29yaW5nLCBtZWRpYW4gZm9s bG93LXVwLCBlZmZlY3Qgc2l6ZXMgd2l0aCBDSSwgYW5kIGV2aWRlbmNlIGFib3V0IHRoZSBt b2RlbCBhc3N1bXB0aW9uLg=="} Which item belongs in the report of a survival analysis? - Median follow-up, events and the proportional-hazards check - Only the p-value of the log-rank test, since it summarises the result - The mean follow-up time of the group of patients who died - The number of patients enrolled, but not the number of events ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - Test PH with **`cox.zph()`** and **plots**; one flagged term among many may be chance - Fix with **`strata()`**, **time-split** or **time-varying** effects - Check **censoring**: how many, who, when; consider sensitivity analyses - Report **events, follow-up, KM with risk table, HRs with CI, PH check, limitations** ::: **Next:** The cheat sheet and the **Dungeons & Dataframes** survival world (coming)

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
